answer: Trust propagates from fixed seed identities through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, so voting influence reflects supported paths, not claimed identities. If a sybil cluster connects to honest nodes only through a sparse external cut, its low conductance, together with capped edge weights, bounds how much seed-derived walk mass can enter it; min-cut transitivity therefore limits its aggregate voting weight. Lantern, cipher, and forge may label test vertices, but confer no trust themselves.
